title.narrative: Multisectoral Needs Assessment 2026 ECHO HIP joint submission with Caritas Germany

description.narrative:
Recent escalations in intercommunal violence and the influx of returnees and refugees from Sudan have placed additional pressure on already overstretched humanitarian services. While there is preliminary information on the needs on ground, and presence of other humanitarian actors, the lack of updated, localized data on the evolving needs, priorities of the affected populations and service gaps in these areas hinders effective planning, prioritization and design of actions in response to the 2026 ECHO Humanitarian Implementation Plan that was recently.
Therefore, CAFOD and Trócaire in Partnership (CTP) proposes a Multisectoral Needs Assessment to generate evidence-based insights into the most urgent needs across sectors. The assessment will be participatory, inclusive, and sensitive to gender, age, and diversity, ensuring that the voices of affected communities guide the response design. It will be conducted by an external consultant with proven experience in leading ECHO-aligned multisectoral needs assessments (MSNAs), and the final report will be tailored to meet the formatting and analytical standards acceptable to ECHO.
Additionally, the needs assessment will be conducted in partnership with Caritas Germany, who will contribute 50% of the required funding for the proposed assessment. This collaboration reflects a broader consortium approach for the proposed 2026 ECHO HIP, in which Caritas Germany will serve as the lead agency, working alongside CAFOD and Trócaire in Partnership (CTP) and two national partners, Agency for Child Relief Aid (ACRA) and African Development Aid (ADA). Within this consortium, ACRA will support the implementation of activities under CTP’s component, while ADA will support those under Caritas Germany’s lead.
